summary: Cathy Cantwell is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Kent (circa 1984–1989). She held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Cecil Bendall was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Oxford, Cambridge, and under Theodor Benfey and Edward Byles Cowell. He served at the British Museum, University College London, and as Professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge.

Cecil Y. Lang studied at Duke University from circa 1937 to 1941. He held posts at Yale University and the University of Chicago before serving as Professor of English at the University of Virginia from circa 1970 to 1991.

Ch'ing-mao Cheng specialized in Sinology and Japanology, earning degrees from National Taiwan University and Princeton. He taught at UC Berkeley and the University of Massachusetts Amherst, later becoming Founding Chair at National Dong Hwa University from circa 1996 to 2003.

Chack-fan Lee, active in Buddhist studies and other fields, studied at The University of Hong Kong and the University of Western Ontario. He served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor of The University of Hong Kong from 1994 to 2015.
Chaeson Kim is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied in the doctoral program at the University of Tokyo (attested 1995) under Ekyo Ejima.

Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Delog Dawa Drolma, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dilgo Khyentse.
Chaim Rabin was a linguist who studied at SOAS and the University of Oxford. He held posts at the University of Oxford from 1941 to 1956 and at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from 1956 to 1986.

Chaisit Suwanvarangkul, working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, conducted research at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi. He served as a Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2015).

Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, earned a doctorate at Oxford and held fellowships at Trinity College, Oxford, and Clare Hall, Cambridge. He later served as professor at Lancaster University (attested 2007–2012).

Chamnong Adivadhanasit, active in Buddhist studies and religious studies, earned a BA from Chulalongkorn University. In 2012, he was attested as a professor at Kasetsart University and a part-time instructor at Chulalongkorn University.
Champa Thupten Zongtse is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who held a post at the University of Göttingen, where he was attested as a lecturer in 2009.
Chandima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Chandrabhāl Tripathi was an Indologist who completed his doctorate under Ernst Waldschmidt at the University of Göttingen. He held posts at Göttingen, Humboldt University of Berlin, and served as Professor of Indology at the Free University of Berlin (circa 1977–1994).
Chang-geun Hwang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000, studying under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and Morten Schlütter.

Changhwan Park is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Otani University and earned a PhD from UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt. He served as a professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2017).

Changpei Luo was a scholar of linguistics and Sinology who studied at Peking University. He held academic posts at Northwest University, Xiamen University, Sun Yat-sen University, and Peking University (circa 1931–1937).

Chanju Mun is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2002) under Charles Hallisey, Morten Schlütter, and Masahiro Shimoda.

Charlene E. Makley is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned her PhD from the University of Michigan in 1999 under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport. She held a post as associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

Charles Alexander Moore was a philosopher who earned his degrees at Yale University. He taught philosophy at Yale before serving as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi from 1936 to 1967 and founding the journal Philosophy East and West.
